welcome: Time itself has stilled: the Great Hourglass is broken, and the world holds its breath.
Stay close to one another, and listen. I will call on you when the tale needs you.

maren.name: Warden Maren
idle: The lamp is steady tonight, and I mean to keep it that way. Go where the story needs you, stranger.
Open your map with M if you lose the thread. I will keep the light.

hale.name: Captain Hale
idle: Quiet on the north road tonight. Too quiet, if you ask me. Quiet is how it starts.
The Watch holds the gate. It is all we can do. You, you can do more. Mind yourself out there.

gruk.name: Gruk, goblin elder
idle: Gruk sits. Gruk listens. At night the bell calls, and Gruk does not answer. Remember that, boy.
The young ones are afraid of you, and they should be a little. But they will remember you did not strike first.

brannoch.name: Brannoch the hermit
idle: The lake keeps still, and so do I. It is a good way to hear what the Vale has left to say.
If you are going to wander, wander toward answers. There are more of them than you would think.

zahra.name: Zahra the sandwalker
idle: The dunes shift while you stand still, and they do not shift the way they used to. Watch your footing.
Water first, then questions. That is the rule of the sand.

voss.name: Sergeant Voss
idle: I was a soldier for thirty years. I am a statue for three. Neither is a good fit.
Keep your blade low and your feet moving. The cold is patient, but it can be outrun.

glimmercap.name: Glimmercap
notes: A glimmercap, glowing softly blue. It is warm to the touch, and something inside it ticks like a tiny heart.

echostone.name: Echo stone
notes: The stone hums under your hand, and an old voice speaks from inside it:
"The Great Hourglass turns, and the Vale turns with it. Seed and harvest, frost and thaw. Every hour has its keeper."
"Someone climbs the Spire stairs at night. He has a clockmaker's hands. He casts no shadow. Do not let him reach the..." The voice breaks off.
The last stone is cracked, and its voice cracks with it:
"It broke. The Hourglass broke into five shards. Whoever holds them holds the hours... But look: a child outside the glass, untouched by it..."

hoursand.name: Hourglass sand
notes: A glittering mound of gold sand. Each grain ticks as it falls, though nothing is falling.

chapters.title: The Stilled Hour
narration: The hour stands still. Seek out Warden Maren in Lanternrest.
intro: Ah, you are the stranger from the crossroads. I am Maren, Warden of Lanternrest, and I have watched the road for you.

Three winters ago, the night the sky cracked, the whole Vale held its breath, and it has not let it out since: clocks stopped, birds fell silent, roads forgot where they led. We call it the Stillness.
I keep the town lamp burning, because a flame that moves is proof that time still does. Help me keep it moving, and I will teach you what I know.

steps.title: The Captain's Wound
steps.hint: Captain Hale rests at the north end of the market square in Lanternrest. Press the action key beside him.
steps.learned: Captain Hale was struck down on the north road by a Shade that wore an apron, like a tradesman.
offer: Before anything else, a man needs your ears. Captain Hale of the Watch took a wound last night, and he will not tell me what struck him. He may tell a stranger.
He sits at the north end of the market. Go and hear him out.
remind: Captain Hale, at the north end of the market square. Go and hear what he has to say.
done: So you are the stranger Maren keeps talking about. Forgive me if I do not stand.

I was on the north road at dusk when something stepped out of the trees. A Shade. It had no shadow of its own, and it wore an apron, of all things, like a tradesman. It touched my arm, and the cold has not left since.
Warmth would help. An Elixir from the apothecary on the square. I have no coin to spare, and I will not pretend I do not need it.

steps.title: Warmth for the Watch
steps.hint: Buy an Elixir at the Apothecary's Shop on the market square in Lanternrest, then bring it to Captain Hale.
steps.learned: The Shade that wounded Captain Hale lurks in the Northern Glade and seems to wait for travellers.
fieldNote: The Elixir is cold in your hand, and so is the air. Somewhere in town, a wounded man is waiting on you.
offer: The Apothecary's Shop, on the square. One Elixir. I will repay you in more than coin: a name, and where to find the thing that did this.
remind: An Elixir from the Apothecary's Shop. My arm will not wait forever.
done: Ah. That is warmer than it has any right to be.
Now listen. It keeps to the Northern Glade, in the Greenwood, where the trees thin and the old path forks. It does not move like the others. It waits. It was waiting for me.
Find it and put it down, before it finds someone who cannot survive it.

steps.title: The Pale Lurker
steps.goal: Defeat the Pale Lurker in the Northern Glade
steps.hint: The Pale Lurker waits in the Northern Glade in the Greenwood, north of the crossroads. It hurls slow bolts, so keep moving and close the distance.
steps.learned: The Pale Lurker's apron bore a stitched name: O. Vale, and a tiny clock face.
fieldNote: The Pale Lurker comes apart like smoke. Where it stood, a scrap of grey apron lies on the grass, stitched with a tiny clock face. It is still ticking.
offer: They call it the Pale Lurker, those who have seen it and lived. It hurls cold, slow bolts, so keep moving, and do not let it keep its distance.
remind: The Pale Lurker, in the Northern Glade in the Greenwood. Keep moving, and close the distance.
done: You came back, and not a scratch on you.
...What is that in your hand? An apron string? Let me see. There is a name stitched into the hem: "O. Vale," and beneath it, a clock face.
Take this to Maren. She will know it.

steps.title: The Name on the Apron
steps.hint: Glimmercaps glow blue in the groves of the Greenwood. Search the area marked on your map.
steps.learned: The apron belonged to Orrin Vale, Keeper of the Great Hourglass: the Shade wore a dead man's clothes.
fieldNote: The third glimmercap pulses once, like a heartbeat, then holds steady. Somewhere beyond the hush, time is still running.
offer: Hale brought me the scrap. The thread is the old kind, the kind the Spire's clockmakers used, and it only shows its story in glimmer light.
Three glimmercaps from the Greenwood groves, and I can read it.
remind: Three glimmercaps, glowing pale blue in the groves of the Greenwood. Touch each one with the action key.
done: Look how the lamp leaps, and look at the thread! Under the glow, the stitching spells out a whole line: "Orrin Vale, Keeper of the Great Hourglass."
Orrin kept the Hourglass. And the thing that wounded Hale was wearing his apron. I do not like that, stranger. I do not like it at all.

chapters.title: Voices in the Stone
narration: Something whispers from the old stones. Follow the voices.
intro: The Hollow wears a dead man's apron. That means this was never random, stranger. Someone did this, or something wearing him did.
The Vale remembers its own story in stone and in the people who stayed. We must go and listen to them, one after another, before the Stillness takes their words too.

steps.title: The Goblin Elder
steps.goal: Speak to Gruk, the goblin elder
steps.hint: Gruk the goblin elder camps at the Old Ruins in the west of the Greenwood. He will not fight you: speak to him with the action key.
steps.learned: A bell tolls from the Spire each night. Those who follow it come back cold and empty, wearing the clothes of men.
offer: The goblins have been fleeing the north for three winters. Their elder, Gruk, camps at the old ruins in the Greenwood, and for once I think a talk would do more than a sword.
Go and listen to him. Listen the whole way through.
remind: Gruk the goblin elder, at the Old Ruins in the Greenwood. Speak to him, do not strike him.
done: You are not hunting me. Good. Sit. Goblins do not bite, not the old ones.

We came south because of the bell. Every night at the same hour a bell tolls from the Spire, and the ones who follow it come back wrong. Cold. Empty. They put on the clothes of men and walk the roads.
There is a hermit by the old lake, Brannoch. He was at the Spire the night of the breaking. Ask him about the Hourglass. And tell him Gruk still owes him a debt.

steps.title: What the Stones Heard
steps.goal: Touch 3 echo stones in the Greenwood
steps.hint: Echo stones stand at the old ruins in the west of the Greenwood, in the Northern Glade and by the Old Lake. Search the areas marked on your map.
steps.learned: The Great Hourglass broke into five shards, and you are untouched by the Stillness: the boy outside time.
fieldNote: The last rune goes dark, but one of them stays faintly warm under your hand. The echo said: a child outside the glass. It was talking about you.
offer: Gruk sent you? That old thief. Then you want the truth, not stories.
I stood at the Spire the night the Hourglass broke. The stones in the Greenwood heard every word, and they speak to anyone who holds still long enough.
Three of them: the old ruins, the glade, the lake. Listen, and then tell me I am a liar.
remind: Three echo stones in the Greenwood: grey pillars carved with runes. Touch each with the action key and listen.
done: You heard it. The five shards. The child outside the glass. Do you understand what you are, boy?
The Stillness cannot hold you. It slides off you like rain. If there is a way to mend the Hourglass, it runs through someone like you.
Go back to Maren and tell her what the stones said. She has been waiting a long time to hear it.

opens.note: The Old Lake has drained, and an iron hatch lies on its bed

steps.title: The Apprentices
steps.goal: Lay 4 skeletons to rest in the Barrow Lands
steps.hint: Brannoch's apprentices walk the Barrow Lands, north of the Greenwood. They throw bone shards from afar, so keep moving, then close in.
steps.learned: The skeletons of the Barrow Lands are Brannoch's lost apprentices, drawn off by the Spire's bell.
fieldNote: The last skeleton folds into a heap of bone, and the air relaxes a little, as if something let go of a held breath.
offer: There is one more thing, and I am ashamed to ask it. The Barrow Lands north of the Greenwood hold my old apprentices. They followed the bell. I cannot reach them, and I will not leave them walking.
Four of them carry the Spire's mark on their ribs. Lay them to rest. Quickly, if you can. Gently, if you must.
remind: Four skeletons in the Barrow Lands, north of the Greenwood. They stay at range and throw bone shards: keep moving, then close in.
done: Four fewer to carry the bell's song. Thank you, boy. I will say their names tonight, one each, and mean it.
A hermit has little to give. This charm was Orrin's. It keeps a body one step ahead of the cold. He would want it to go to you.

chapters.title: The Fallen Sand
narration: Beyond the green, the sand has begun to swallow what was once safe.
intro: The Hourglass did not simply break. It scattered. Where its sand fell, the Stillness is thickest, and it has set guards over every place it fell.
Whatever is behind this is gathering the pieces, and it moves faster than we do. We have to find them first, which means going where the guards are.

steps.title: The Sandwalker
steps.goal: Speak to Zahra at the Oasis
steps.hint: Zahra the sandwalker waits at the Oasis in the Sunscar Desert, far to the north-west past the Greenwood.
steps.learned: Every grain of Hourglass sand leans north, toward the Spire.
offer: Brannoch's word has weight with me. Now we must find where the pieces went. There is a sandwalker, Zahra, at the oasis in the Sunscar Desert, far to the north-west. She reads the grains.
Go and ask her what they say. Take the long road, and drink before you thirst.
remind: Zahra the sandwalker, at the Oasis in the Sunscar Desert, far to the north-west.
done: A stranger, in this heat, asking about sand! Good. Most ask me about water.
The sand that fell when the Hourglass broke is still out here, in mounds that glitter. Every grain of it leans north, even lying still. Toward the Spire.
Maren sent this with a trader, for the cold nights out here. Her mother's mantle: it mends what the cold bites. Now sit, and I will tell you what I need.

steps.title: Grains of the Hourglass
steps.goal: Gather 4 mounds of hourglass sand in the Sunscar Desert
steps.hint: Hourglass sand lies scattered across the Sunscar Desert, far to the north-west. Raiders and worse guard the dunes. Search the areas marked on your map.
steps.learned: The Hourglass sand points toward the Frozen Ledge in the Frostlands, where a shard fell.
fieldNote: Every grain you hold tilts the same way, east and north, like a compass needle. Far off, a bell tolls once, and the sand goes still.
offer: Bring me four pinches of the glitter from the dunes. I can read where the shard that fell here went, and where its twin fell. Mind the raiders. And the ticking.
Press the action key beside each glittering mound.
remind: Four glittering mounds of hourglass sand in the Sunscar Desert. Mind the raiders.
done: Now hold still. Watch the grains...
They all lean east, to the Frozen Ledge in the Frostlands. A shard fell there, and something stands guard.

But first the orcs. Their captain carries a banner that ticks. Do not call it a banner. It is a piece of the Hourglass frame, and he marches to it. Take it down. These boots are a sandwalker's. They will not let you sink.

steps.title: The Ticking Banner
steps.goal: Defeat Tusk-Captain Urgath in the Sunscar Desert
steps.hint: Tusk-Captain Urgath stands near the Ring of Stones in the Sunscar Desert. He hits hard and shrugs off stagger: hit, step back, hit again.
steps.learned: The Stillness commands through objects: a ticking banner moves the orcs like puppets.
fieldNote: Urgath falls with his banner still clenched in his fist. The ticking stops. In the new silence you realise it was the only sound keeping time out here.
offer: His name is Urgath. He stands near the Ring of Stones with the banner. Orcs march when he marches. Cut the banner down and the others may remember they are free.
He does not flinch when struck, so do not trade blows: hit, step away, hit again.
remind: Tusk-Captain Urgath, near the Ring of Stones in the Sunscar Desert. He does not flinch, so hit and step away.
done: The banner is silent at last. Look: a clock hand set in the shaft, stopped at the hour the Hourglass broke.
The Stillness commands through things like this. Whoever holds the pieces holds the orcs, the frozen soldiers, everything. Go east, to the Frozen Ledge. I will stay and keep watch on the dunes.
Take the captain's helm. He will not be needing it, and it is surprisingly good at finding coin.

chapters.title: The Frozen March
narration: North, the cold marches south to meet you. Go warily.
intro: The road to the Spire runs through the cold east, and the cold east is where the Stillness has marched its soldiers.
This is the last I can ask of you for now, and the hardest. After it, we will know who we are really fighting.

steps.title: The Frozen Ledge
steps.goal: Reach the Frozen Ledge in the Frostlands
steps.hint: The Frozen Ledge lies in the far east of the Frostlands, along the town road east of Lanternrest. Search the area marked on your map.
steps.learned: The soldiers of the Spire Guard are not enemies. They are frozen men, still awake inside.
fieldNote: Soldiers stand in the snow in perfect ranks, mid-march, frost on their eyelashes. Not one of them blinks. Not one, except the sergeant at the front, whose eyes follow you, wide and terribly alive.
offer: Now the last stretch, and the hardest. The sand leans east to the Frozen Ledge in the Frostlands, along the town road. A shard fell there, and the Stillness marched its soldiers to guard it.
Go and look. Only look, at first. Come back, if you must. But I think you will want to hear what they have to say.
remind: The Frozen Ledge in the far east of the Frostlands, along the town road east of Lanternrest.
done: You... you move. You breathe. You are the first thing in three winters that has.
I am Sergeant Voss, of the Spire Guard. We were marching to the Spire the night the bell first tolled. We reached the ledge. The cold took us all, but it did not take our minds.
We are not your enemies. We are prisoners. Come closer. I have a great deal to tell you, and very little time before the bell calls again.

steps.title: Peace for the Spire Guard
steps.hint: The frozen soldiers walk the Frostlands, east of Lanternrest. They do not flinch, so strike, step back, and strike again.
steps.learned: Defeating a frostbound frees the man inside: the Spire Guard can be given peace.
fieldNote: Where the last frostbound falls, snow begins to drift again. For a moment the flakes fall instead of hanging. Then the hush returns.
offer: The ones who fell to the bell are on the ice now, mindless, marching in circles. They were my men. I cannot reach them. You can.
Four of them. It is not murder: the cold is all that is left in them, and when it breaks they are free. Do it quickly, and say their names if you know them.
remind: Four frostbound in the Frostlands, east of Lanternrest. They do not flinch, so strike, step back, and strike again.
done: I felt it. Each one. Like a knot coming undone in my own chest. Thank you.
This cuirass was my captain's. It was warmed at the town lamp once, long ago, and it has not forgotten. Wear it, and carry his warmth into the last of this.
One thing remains. The shard itself. A troll in the Frostlands swallowed it, and the cold has made the troll into its heart.

steps.title: The Stillheart
steps.goal: Defeat the Stillheart in the Frostlands
steps.hint: The Stillheart prowls the Frostlands near Mirrorfrost Lake. It is huge, slow and cannot be stunned: keep your distance, bring potions, and take your time.
steps.learned: A shard of the Hourglass bears a name: Orrin, Clockmaker. Four shards remain, and the Stillness knows yours.
fieldNote: The Stillheart's heavy hand opens, and a splinter of glass rolls out, warm, ticking. Take it to Maren in Lanternrest.
offer: It is called the Stillheart now. It lives near Mirrorfrost Lake. It is huge and slow and it cannot be stunned. Bring potions, and take your time.
Bring me down that thing, and bring the shard to Maren. She will know what to do with what is written on it.
remind: The Stillheart, near Mirrorfrost Lake in the Frostlands. Bring potions. When it falls, take the shard to Maren in Lanternrest.
done: A shard of the Hourglass. It is warm, and it ticks. I hold it to the lamp, and the flame stands perfectly still.
There is a name scratched into the splinter: "Orrin, Clockmaker." The keeper of the Spire. The one whose apron the Shade wore.
He did not break the Vale, stranger. He was the first thing the Stillness took, and it still wears him.
Four shards remain, and the Stillness knows your name now. Keep this pendant close and keep moving. We will speak again when the next shard calls.

chapters.title: Beneath the Vale
narration: The Vale has deeps of its own, and each has a king. Go down, and put them out.
intro: The Stillheart is down, but the Stillness has roots under the Vale: the vaults below Lanternrest, the barrows under the graveyard, and the hollow under the dunes.
Each has someone who sits at the bottom of it. I would see all three put out before the next shard calls.

steps.title: Lamps Under the Market
steps.goal: Drive off 3 hexers in the Drowned Cistern
steps.hint: The drain in the market square leads down to the Lanternrest Sewers. A stair in the north-east room goes on to the Lanternrest Undercroft, where hexers tend the lanterns.
steps.learned: The lamps lost from Lanternrest are burning in the vaults beneath the market, tended by hexers. Someone is keeping them warm.
offer: The lamp is steady, but the lamplighters keep losing lamps, oil and all. The drain in the market hums at night, and the hum is in tune.
Go down through the market drain, and past the sewers to the Undercroft. Hexers tend the lanterns there. Drive off three, and see who they serve.
remind: Three hexers in the Drowned Cistern, under the market drain. The stair is in the north-east room of the sewers.
done: Three hexers, and every one with a ledger of streets. They were taking the lamps in order, like a harvest.
There is a throne of lamp-frames in the chapel beyond the cistern. Whatever sits on it is the one who counts the lamps.

opens.note: The hexers' barricades have come down: the way to the Drowned Throne is open

steps.title: The Cistern King
steps.goal: Defeat the Cistern King in the Undercroft
steps.hint: The Cistern King sits among the stolen lanterns beyond the Forgotten Chapel in the Lanternrest Undercroft. He is huge: keep your distance, bring potions, and strike when his swing is spent.
steps.learned: A troll made a throne of the town's lamp-frames under the market. With him gone the drains are quiet, and the lamps stay lit.
fieldNote: The King falls with a sound like a cistern emptying. Around the chapel, every lantern gutters at once, and then, one by one, burns steady.
offer: A troll took the old cistern for a court, and he has been opening and closing the town's doors for months. I want him put out like one of his lamps.
He is big and he is proud. Bring potions, and do not stand where he swings.
remind: The Cistern King, on his throne of lamp-frames in the Undercroft beneath Lanternrest. Bring potions.
done: The hum stopped an hour ago. I felt it go, like a held breath let out. The lamplighters are counting their lamps twice over, to be sure.
This charm was a drainwarden's, long before the town forgot there were drains. Wear it, and carry on. The dead of the Barrow Lands have been restless since the bell.

steps.title: The Watch Below
steps.goal: Lay 3 wraiths to rest in the Barrow Deep
steps.hint: A tomb in the Barrow Lands graveyard is a door down into the Barrow Deep. The wraiths walk the Ossuary, past the Foyer of Names.
steps.learned: The first watchman of the Barrow Lands still keeps his post below the graveyard, and the dead who serve him do not rest.
offer: The bell does not only call the living. Below the graveyard in the Barrow Lands there is a deep where the first watchman still keeps his post, and his watch will not end.
Go down by the tomb, through the Foyer of Names and the Ossuary. Lay three of his wraiths to rest, and see the watchman for yourself.
remind: Three wraiths in the Barrow Deep, past the Foyer of Names. The way down is the tomb in the Barrow Lands graveyard.
done: Three wraiths. Their names were cut over the door, once, and their faces were never cut anywhere. Perhaps now they rest.
The watchman waits at the deepest gate, still guarding a road that has long since been forgotten. He does not know the watch is over. Someone must tell him.

steps.title: The Pale Warden
steps.goal: Defeat the Pale Warden in the Barrow Deep
steps.hint: The Pale Warden stands at the deepest gate of the Barrow Deep, past the Ossuary. He is tall and he hits hard after a long wind-up: step back from the swing, then strike.
steps.learned: The watchman of the Barrow Lands has been relieved at last. The dead below the graveyard keep no more post.
offer: He was the first to stand watch over the barrows, and he stands it still. He will not yield to words, so end his watch gently, and with your blade.
He swings slow and hard. Watch the wind-up, and step back from it.
remind: The Pale Warden, at the deepest gate of the Barrow Deep, below the graveyard of the Barrow Lands.
done: The ground is quiet. For the first time in three winters the barrow wind has dropped, and the old stones are only stones.
His helm. It kept a watchman's thoughts on the long dark, and it will keep yours. Take it. The sand has troubles of its own: Zahra has been asking after you.

steps.title: The Furnace Hall
steps.goal: Drive off 3 trolls in the Sunscar Depths
steps.hint: A cave mouth in the Sunscar Desert leads down to the Sunscar Hollow, and deeper into the Sunscar Depths: the Furnace Hall and the Gallery of Bones. Trolls hold the lower halls.
steps.learned: An orc king sits on a forgotten throne beneath the Sunscar, and the trolls of the Furnace Hall serve the fire that answered him.
offer: There is a hollow under the dunes where the orcs go and do not come back. The fire down there has answered something, and the trolls that serve it have grown bold.
Go down by the cave mouth, past the Hollow, into the Furnace Hall. Drive off three trolls, and mind the heat: drink before you thirst.
remind: Three trolls in the Sunscar Depths, beyond the Furnace Hall. The way down is the cave mouth in the Sunscar Desert.
done: Three trolls, and the hall is quieter. Not quiet. There is a throne at the far end that the fire still leans toward.
An orc king, Ashmaw, sits on it. He has sat there until the fire answered, and it is not fond of strangers. Rest, drink, and be ready.

steps.title: Ashmaw, the Hollow King
steps.goal: Defeat Ashmaw in the Sunscar Depths
steps.hint: Ashmaw sits on the throne at the end of the Gallery of Bones in the Sunscar Depths. He is a king in a furnace: bring antidotes for the burn, potions, and room to move.
steps.learned: The Hollow King has fallen, and the fire under the Sunscar has gone out. The Vale's three deeps are quiet.
fieldNote: The throne cracks. Below it, the furnace dims, and the heat leaves the stone like a sigh. For the first time, the Hollow is cool.
offer: He has sat there so long that the fire answers to him. That is not a king. That is a wound in the sand, and it needs closing.
Take everything you have. Then go down, and come back and tell Maren it is done: she has been keeping count.
remind: Ashmaw, the Hollow King, on his throne at the end of the Sunscar Depths. Then Maren in Lanternrest.
done: It is done, then. The cistern, the barrow, and the hollow under the sand. Zahra's runner came ahead of you, breathless.
This is Ashmaw's own hide, and it is yours. You will not want for armour again, nor for work: the Vale is a long road.

epics.title: The Greenwood Reckoning
epics.tagline: Drive the creatures out of the Greenwood and the woods beyond it, one lair at a time.
epics.opening: The woods around Lanternrest have grown bold. Something is driving the creatures out of the dark, and they are coming for the road. Meet them first.
epics.ending: The woods are quiet again. The creatures that came out of the dark have gone back to it, or gone for good.

steps.tell: The goblins in {area} were the first to come out of the trees. Thin them, and the rest will think twice.
The wolfkin follow the goblins like a bad smell. Drive them off before they find the road.
Whatever woke the dead in {area} is the reason for all of it. Put them to rest, and the woods may settle.

epics.title: The Barrow Vigil
epics.tagline: The watch outpost in the Barrow Lands stopped sending word. The dead have not.
epics.opening: Lanternrest's watch posts a rider to the Barrow Lands every week. Last week the rider came back with a bone in his saddlebag, and no memory of finding it.
epics.ending: The outpost's lamp is lit again, and the barrows are quiet. The watchman wrote your names on the lintel, below the names of those who did not come home.

steps.tell: The rider's trail starts at the graveyard in {area}. Walk it, and see what he stopped to look at.
aftermath: Fresh earth on old graves, and a single iron nail in each. Someone is marking the dead, and not for respect.

steps.tell: The marked dead are rising in {area}. Lay them back down, and mind the arrows.
aftermath: The bones are warm to the touch. They were not raised long ago. Whatever woke them is still close.

steps.tell: The watch outpost lies in {area}. The roof is down, but the lamp might not be. Go and look.
aftermath: The last page of the watch ledger reads, in a steady hand: 'They are not attacking. They are waiting.'

steps.tell: The waiting ones shamble at the edge of {area}. They have been standing there all week. Put them to rest.
aftermath: One wears a watchman's coat, buttoned wrong, the lamp-oil flask still on its belt. Somebody should write his family.

steps.tell: The marks all point to the chasm in {area}. Go to its edge, and see what the dead have been waiting for.
aftermath: Far below, a light, patient and blue. It does not flicker. The dead face it like a congregation at prayer.

epics.title: The Sunscar Legion
epics.tagline: A legion that was never disbanded still holds the mesa, and still takes tolls.
epics.opening: The caravans cross the Sunscar by the Watch Post road. This season, someone is collecting tolls there in an orc legion's name. The legion fell a hundred years ago.
epics.ending: The tollkeepers lay down their arms, and the mesa's banner comes down. Whatever the legion was guarding, it is the desert's again, and the caravans pay nothing.

steps.tell: The caravan masters meet at the post in {area}. Go there, and hear what the toll costs them.
aftermath: The ledger shows tolls in silver, receipts stamped with a legion seal nobody has cut since the old king's day.

steps.tell: The toll collectors ride out from {area}. They wear the legion's colours badly. Break them.
aftermath: They carry good steel and bad manners. Someone armed them, and someone fed them. A legion needs a quartermaster.

steps.tell: The orders come from the mesa in {area}. Climb it, and see who is giving them.
aftermath: On the mesa, the barracks are swept. Beds made, boots in rows. Whoever lives here is keeping a promise.

steps.tell: The mesa's guard is a warband of true orcs in {area}. Break them, and the toll road is yours.
aftermath: A captain dies clutching a locket. Inside: 'Hold until relieved.' Relieved by whom, after a hundred years?

steps.tell: The old orders came from the temple in {area}. Go in, and tell whatever waits there that the war is over.
aftermath: Inside, a mummy's hand rests on a bronze horn. It has waited a century for someone to blow the retreat.

epics.title: The Drowned Road
epics.tagline: The causeway through the Gloamfen Marsh is sinking, and something is sinking it.
epics.opening: The only dry road between the jungle and the frost runs through Gloamfen Marsh. It has dropped a foot a week since midsummer. The road crews say the marsh is breathing in.
epics.ending: The causeway rises, stone by stone, and holds. The marsh has not forgiven you, but it has agreed to leave the road alone.

steps.tell: The marsh begins in the Mirewater, in {area}. Go to the pools, and see what the crews saw.
aftermath: The pools are clear as glass, and the water is rising against the slope. Whatever pulls the marsh down feeds it up here.

steps.tell: The hexers in {area} have been dragging stones into the water. Stop them before they finish whatever they are building.
aftermath: A hexer's satchel holds a map of the causeway, every post crossed out in red. This was not mischief. It was a survey.

steps.tell: The first sunken stretch is in {area}. Walk it, and mark what the marsh has already taken.
aftermath: The stones are pulled down in a line, as if by a rope. There is a drag mark in the mud, wide as a wagon.

steps.tell: Something rises from the water around {area} to guard the drag. Put the bog ghouls down.
aftermath: They wore charms of bone and reed, stitched with the hexers' red thread. They were a workforce, and the marsh the employer.

steps.tell: The drag leads to the island in {area}. Go there, and meet whatever wants the road under the water.
aftermath: A troll the size of a barn sleeps beside a heap of causeway stones, each one numbered. It has been building something, post by post.

epics.title: The Frost That Stays
epics.tagline: The deep Frostlands have stopped thawing, and the thaw was the only promise the north ever made.
epics.opening: Every spring the Frostlands thaw a little further south. This spring they did not. The herders say the cold has a will now, and a captain.
epics.ending: The ice on the ledge cracks, and water runs downhill for the first time in a year. The frost is only patient again. Spring will come late, and herders will name children after you.

steps.tell: The herders gather at the cross field in {area}. Go there, and hear what they have seen walking the ice.
aftermath: The herders whisper of a figure in a great helm who stands at the lake and does not breathe.

steps.tell: The frostbound patrol the road in {area}, as if the road were theirs. Take it back from them.
aftermath: Each has a fresh rime of frost on its ribs, and a blue light in its eye socket. It is spreading from somewhere north.

steps.tell: The cold seeps from the lake in {area}. Go to its shore and see what the ice reflects.
aftermath: The lake reflects a night of stars in the middle of the afternoon. The cold is looking at you.

steps.tell: The great brutes at the lake's edge in {area} have been fed on something. Strike them down before they find the road.
aftermath: The creatures are heavier than they should be, their fur dense as fleece. Something has been feeding them cold.

steps.tell: The wardens of the frozen ledge march in {area}, in the captain's name. Break the guard.
aftermath: The captain's great helm lies in the snow, empty. The cold has a will, and the will has moved on.

steps.tell: The cold's last stand is on the ledge in {area}. Climb it, and end the winter that will not end.
aftermath: The ledge cracks. The sky clears. Somewhere south, a herder looks at a dripping icicle and forgets what she was afraid of.

epics.title: Under Lanternrest
epics.tagline: The lamplighters keep losing lamps. The town was built over something that wants the light.
epics.opening: Every dusk the lamplighters of Lanternrest find another lantern gone, oil and all. The market drain has begun to hum at night. The watch says it is the wind. The wind does not hum in tune.
epics.ending: The hum stops, and the lamps stay lit. Below the market, the Cistern King's court stands empty, and the town sleeps over a quiet vault. The lamplighters still count their lamps, twice, to be sure.

steps.tell: Begin where the lamps go: the market drain, and the sewers under it in {area}. Go down, and see what the lamplighters will not.
aftermath: Lantern glass, swept into neat piles along the walkway. Not scattered. Collected. Someone down here is keeping count.

steps.tell: The drowned walk the sewers of {area}, each with a lantern-hook in its fist. Put them down, and mind the water.
aftermath: Each hook is bound with fresh oiled twine. The dead did not do this alone. Someone gave them a purpose, and a uniform.
A stair behind the north-east room, newly unbarred, breathes cold air. The sewers were never the bottom.

steps.tell: The stair leads to vaults older than the town, in {area}. Walk to the cistern, and see where the oil goes.
aftermath: The cistern is ringed with lanterns, lit and burning, hundreds of them. The water at the centre glows green under them. Something is being kept warm.

steps.tell: The hexers tending the cistern's lanterns will not leave their charge. Drive them off in {area}.
aftermath: A hexer's ledger lists every lamp by street name, and which streets will go dark next. They were being taken in order, like a harvest.

steps.tell: A chapel older than Lanternrest lies at the west end of {area}. The lamps were carried there. Go and see why.
aftermath: The chapel's altar bears a throne of stacked lamp-frames, and a plaque: 'In the dark, a king keeps his court.' The plaque is old. The lamps are not.

steps.tell: The court's bodyguard, bloated ghouls dressed in lamplighters' coats, hold the way south in {area}. Break them.
aftermath: Under the coats, hooks and keys: every drain in town is on one ring. The king has been opening and closing the town's doors for months.

steps.tell: The Cistern King sits among the stolen lights in {area}, sure of his court. Put out his fire.
aftermath: The King falls and the cistern's glow gutters. Overhead, the lamps of Lanternrest steady one by one, as if someone had stopped blowing on them.

epics.title: The Barrow Deep
epics.tagline: The watchman who never left his post is still counting. He has reached your name.
epics.opening: The Barrow Vigil ended with a light in a chasm and a congregation of dead. This season a tomb at the back of the graveyard stands open, and the watch ledger has a new last line, in an old hand: 'Relief expected.'
epics.ending: The Pale Warden lays down his sword, and the Barrow Lands exhale. The tomb stair is sealed from within. The ledger's last line is crossed out, and under it, in steadier ink: 'Relieved.'

steps.tell: The tomb at the back of the graveyard in {area} stands open. Start there, and see what the Vigil left behind.
aftermath: Fresh footprints lead down the tomb's stair, and none lead back. Someone walked in, in good boots, with purpose.

steps.tell: The dead above the tomb are stirring in {area}, rising in ranks, not heaps. Cut them down before they march.
aftermath: They fall in neat rows, shields still in hand. Drilled. Whoever is below taught them to die in formation.

steps.tell: Go down the tomb's stair to {area}. A hundred names are cut into its walls. Find the newest.
aftermath: The newest name is a watchman's, from last year. Under it, a tally, in the same hand: one stroke for every night he has kept the post.

steps.tell: The long hall of {area} is thick with the unburied, each wearing a scrap of watch coat. Walk through them.
aftermath: Every scrap carries the same stitched badge: a tower above a lantern. They are not wandering. They are on patrol.

steps.tell: The south road runs through the ossuary in {area}. Go on, and read what the walls of bone say.
aftermath: The skulls are stacked by rank, captains to cadets. A gap in the wall waits for one more. The mortar around it is fresh.

steps.tell: The ossuary's guard still holds its post in {area}, and will not stand down for strangers. Break the ranks.
aftermath: A broken captain's helm rolls from the heap. Inside, scratched with a dagger: 'He will not leave until someone relieves him. Someone must.'

steps.tell: The watch's casters keep the seat in {area}, and have kept it a long time. Silence them before the Warden hears you.
aftermath: The wraiths fall, and a deep voice from the south chamber says, without anger: 'Are you my relief?' It does not wait for an answer.

steps.tell: The Pale Warden stands in his seat in {area}, sword drawn, keeping a post that ended centuries ago. Relieve him.
aftermath: He kneels at the end, sword across his knees. 'Post relieved,' he says. 'Tell them I held it.' The dust that settles on him has a peaceful sound.

epics.title: The Sunscar Depths
epics.tagline: Under the desert's cave, a furnace has a king, and he has noticed the surface.
epics.opening: The desert's cave was always a goblin's den. This year the sand above it is warm, and caravans report an orc banner no clan will own. Something under the hollow is waking, and it is hungry for the sky.
epics.ending: The Furnace Hall cools, and the sand above it goes cold for the first time in a season. Ashmaw's throne cracks down its middle, and the desert wind carries the smell of ash for a day, then forgets it. The caravans pass untaxed.

steps.tell: Start at the cave mouth in the dunes of {area}, where the sand is warm. Go to the Hollow, and see what the desert is hiding.
aftermath: The cave's walls are warm, and the shaft of daylight at the foyer shows a haze of soot in the air. Something below is burning, and burning well.

steps.tell: Orc scouts hold the hollow's deeper tunnel in {area}, bound with the king's red cord. Clear them, and the way down is open.
aftermath: Each scout wears the same red cord, knotted in the same pattern. A uniform of rank. Whatever is below has an army, and it keeps accounts.

steps.tell: The tunnel drops into the Sunscar Depths, in {area}. Cross to the Furnace Hall, and look at the lava with your own eyes.
aftermath: A lake of lava, ringed by a path worn smooth by a thousand marching feet. The heat is a wall. Beyond it, a drum beats, slow as a heart.

steps.tell: Mummies, old as the sand, stand guard along the Furnace Hall in {area}. They have been paid in something other than gold. Put them down.
aftermath: Each carries a scroll in a language you cannot read, sealed with the king's red wax. They are not guards. They are witnesses to a contract.

steps.tell: The west road runs through the Gallery of Bones in {area}. Go in, and read what the king keeps on his walls.
aftermath: The walls are carved with a calendar, one date circled in red: the first of next month. Beneath it, carvings of the sky, and a hand reaching up.

steps.tell: The gallery's dead are still marching in {area}, in step with the drum. Break their ranks before the king calls them to the surface.
aftermath: The last of them drops a banner, torn, red on black. Pinned to it, a map of the caravan road, with watchtowers marked. The king is planning a war.

steps.tell: The king's bodyguard, great trolls in iron, hold the seat's doors in {area}. Take them down, and the way to Ashmaw is clear.
aftermath: The last troll drops a key of black iron, hot to the touch. The seat's doors open to it, and the drum stops, as if a held breath had been let go.

steps.tell: Ashmaw, the Hollow King, sits on a throne that has been warm for a thousand years, and rises to meet you in {area}. End his reign.
aftermath: The throne splits, and a cold wind comes down the shaft for the first time in an age. The king never wanted a kingdom. He wanted the sky.

epics.title: Ash and Ember
epics.tagline: Past the Mirewater the map runs out, and what burns there has been waiting for a visitor.
epics.opening: Beyond the Mirewater the old maps show a smudge and a word: 'burnt'. This season the smudge has grown a road, and a banner no one raised. Something in the Emberwaste is drawing the legions of the dead into line.
epics.ending: Vharek falls, and the Cinder Ziggurat's fire sinks to embers. The Emberwaste will burn on for a thousand years, but it burns without a will now, and the road east is only a road.

steps.tell: Cross the Mirewater to the burnt road in {area}. Go to the gate, and see the first land past the old maps.
aftermath: The gate is a pair of blackened trees, and between them a milestone, new: 'Cinder Ziggurat, 40 leagues.' Someone has been laying road.

steps.tell: Orc pickets hold the road in {area}, in the red cord of a king who is not yet named. Break them.
aftermath: Each carries the same crude brand on the shield: a flame inside a ring. Whoever they follow does not mind being worshipped.

steps.tell: The road bends past lakes of lava in {area}. Go to the shore, and see what they feed.
aftermath: The lava lakes are stirred into slow spirals, all turning one way. Under the heat shimmer, something vast breathes in time with them.

steps.tell: Embalmed sentries stand in the ash round {area}, where no one buried them. Lay them down.
aftermath: The wrappings are new, soaked in oil and sealed with a flame-mark. Someone is making mummies, and sending them to guard the road.

steps.tell: A war camp of the dead lies in {area}. Walk to it, and read the crosses before you fight.
aftermath: Four hundred iron crosses, each with a unit number and a date, the same date. A legion that all died on the same day, and was not allowed to rest.

steps.tell: The legion's war-trolls drag the dead's wagons in {area}. Put them down, and the camp falls quiet.
aftermath: The wagons carry banners folded and numbered, one for each cross in the field. Someone means to march them somewhere, and soon.

steps.tell: The banners all point to the Ziggurat in {area}. Climb to its steps, and meet whatever has been gathering a legion.
aftermath: The Ziggurat's steps are warm as a living thing. At its top, a throne of cooled lava, and the shape of a man, kneeling, burning without burning.

steps.tell: Vharek, the Cinderlord, rises from his throne in {area}, and the legion's drum goes silent to watch. End him.
aftermath: The fire falls out of him like a robe. Underneath, an old soldier, who says only: 'Was it a good war?' He does not wait for an answer either.

epics.title: The Long White
epics.tagline: Beyond the Frostlands the snow has stopped falling and started to stand.
epics.opening: The herders always kept to their side of the white, where the snow falls. This winter it stopped falling and started to stand, in pillars, in rows, in the shape of men. Something is raising an army out of the weather.
epics.ending: The Hoarfather falls, and the standing snow slumps into plain drifts. The wind, for the first time in a year, blows from somewhere that is not the north. Rimeheart is a land again, and not an army.

steps.tell: Past the Frostlands the snow does not move. Go to the pillars in {area}, and see where the herders turn back.
aftermath: Two columns of packed snow, taller than a house, each with a face. The faces are not carved. They grew.

steps.tell: The standing snow has bones in it, and they walk in {area}. Break the first rank.
aftermath: They fall in sheets of ice, and under each, a coat of the Frostlands' own watch. The army was raised from those who went looking.

steps.tell: The cold is deepest at the lakes in {area}. Walk the shore, and see how far down the ice goes.
aftermath: The ice is clear to the bottom, where rows of figures stand on the lakebed, looking up, waiting for a thaw that will not come.

steps.tell: Yeti herds the size of barns graze the lake shore in {area}, fattened on something cold. Cull them.
aftermath: Their fur is full of needles of ice, glittering. They were not born. They were poured, into a shape, and told to keep the herd.

steps.tell: The snow forms ranks in the field in {area}. Walk to it, and look the army in the face.
aftermath: Ten thousand pillars in lines to the horizon, all facing one way. At the end of the lines, a hill, and on the hill, a throne of ice.

steps.tell: The wardens of the ice throne stand picket at the field in {area}, in the Hoarfather's name. Take their line.
aftermath: The last warden's helm rolls and shatters. Inside, a note in frozen ink: 'He does not want war. He wants to be remembered.'

steps.tell: The throne stands in the old halls of {area}, among the plateau's pillars. Climb to it, and answer the Hoarfather's summons.
aftermath: The halls are older than the snow, one winter carved on every pillar. The last pillar is blank. He is waiting for the carver.

steps.tell: The Hoarfather stands on the Wyrm's Rest in {area}, tall as the hall, and bows his head to you, as to a challenger. Meet him.
aftermath: He falls slowly, the way a drift settles. The pillars of the field crumble to powder in a long sigh, and the sun, for a moment, is a visitor.

epics.title: Salt and Glass
epics.tagline: Past the Emberwaste the sand has turned to glass, and the glass has begun to remember.
epics.opening: East of the Emberwaste the desert is not sand but glass, fused in one night by a fire nobody saw. Caravans that cross it come back with their water bright as mirrors and their drivers silent. Something there keeps a court.
epics.ending: The Glass Sovereign shatters, and the whole waste rings once, like a struck bell, and is quiet. The dunes will drift back over the glass in a century. Until then, the caravans cross with their eyes open, and their drivers talk.

steps.tell: Cross out of the Emberwaste to the pale edge of {area}. Go to the gate, and see where the ash gives way to glass.
aftermath: The ash stops at a line as straight as a ruler. Beyond it, the ground is white and smooth, and every footprint stays, bright as a coin.

steps.tell: Raiders in glass-bright armour ride the Salt Flats of {area}, taxing whoever crosses. Ride them down.
aftermath: Their armour is glass, grown on them, and it rings when struck. They did not buy it. They were given it, by someone who wants them seen.

steps.tell: The flats of {area} are where the caravans vanish. Walk out to the middle, and look at the ground.
aftermath: Under the glass, inches down, the shapes of wagons, oxen and drivers, fused mid-stride. The flats are a collection.

steps.tell: Sand-wrapped sentries pace the glass of {area}, and cast no shadows. Put them down.
aftermath: Their wrappings are woven of the caravans' own canvas. Someone is dressing the dead in the lost, and standing them in rows.

steps.tell: The biggest caravan of all lies in {area}. Go to the ring of broken pillars, and see what the king keeps there.
aftermath: Pillars ring a wagon of black glass. Inside, a throne of caravan chests, and carved on a pillar, a name from the Barrow ledgers.

steps.tell: Glass-skinned trolls haul the king's treasure through {area}. Strike them down, and take the road.
aftermath: They shatter, and under the glass are plain trolls, weeping. The glass was grown on them alive. They have asked to be let out ever since.

steps.tell: The road ends at the citadel in {area}. Climb to its gate, and meet the court.
aftermath: The citadel's floor is a lake of white fire gone still. On the throne, a figure in a crown of the same glass is rising.

steps.tell: The Glass Sovereign rises from his glass throne in {area}, crowned in what the fire made of his kingdom. End his reign.
aftermath: The crown cracks first, then the sky seems to, and he sighs, a sound like wind in a bottle. 'At last,' he says. 'Something that breaks.'

epics.title: The Sunken Crown
epics.tagline: A kingdom drowned a thousand years ago, and its king never agreed to it.
epics.opening: East of Rimeheart the land goes under: black pools, standing towers, a throne hall up to its knees in water. The drowned kingdom's king has been seen at the surface, wearing a crown and wading toward the road.
epics.ending: The Drowned King sinks, crown last, and the moor goes still for the first time in a thousand years. The towers still stand, but they look like towers now, not a court. Somewhere under the pools, a kingdom agrees to be over.

steps.tell: Cross out of the white to the first black water of {area}. Go to the gate, and read the line where frost meets flood.
aftermath: The snow stops, and the water begins, with no mud between. A signpost stands in the pool, and its arm points down.

steps.tell: Drowned footmen in rotted livery wade the shallows of {area}. Send them back under.
aftermath: Each wears the same livery, a gold crown on blue, bleached to grey. They are still on duty. They have been on duty for a thousand years.

steps.tell: The pools of {area} are all one water. Walk their bank, and see what lies at the bottom.
aftermath: The pools are clear as ink and deep as wells. Down at the bottom, a road, paved, and on the road, lamp-posts, lit, in a row going the same way as you.

steps.tell: The King's witches keep the pools in {area}, singing the water high. Silence them.
aftermath: A hymn is carved on a post: 'Rise, rise, the king's drowned court.' They are not drowning the land. They are raising a kingdom.

steps.tell: The tallest tower stands alone in {area}. Wade to it, and see what the court keeps in its cellar.
aftermath: The tower's door is under the water, and its top is a bell chamber. The bell is alive with a sound you cannot hear, only feel in the teeth: a summons.

steps.tell: The King's guard, great trolls in green iron, stand in the shallows of {area}. Take them down.
aftermath: The last guard drops a key of drowned gold. His breastplate reads: Captain of the Gate. He guarded it from the day it went under.

steps.tell: The throne hall rises from the water in {area}. Wade in, and hear the court assemble.
aftermath: The hall is full: the drowned, waist-deep, in ranks, every face turned to the throne. A voice from the water says: 'The audience is granted.'

steps.tell: The Drowned King rises from the water of {area}, crowned in weeds, and holds his court for the last time. End it.
aftermath: He sinks, crown last, and says only: 'Dismissed.' The drowned lower their heads together and go under, like a tide finally told it may.

epilogue: The lamp burns steadier than it has in three winters, and that is your doing, and Hale's, and Gruk's, and Brannoch's, and Zahra's, and Voss's. The Vale remembers who helped.
Four shards are still out there, and something that wears Orrin's hands is still walking the Spire stairs. But the Vale is not lost.
Rest, stranger. The next part of this story is still being written.
